quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will stay in your lane.
It is safe because motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast may cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot.
Use only your mirrors to see all around you.
Point in the direction you are turning.
Speed up to pass other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: What should you do if the front wheel locks up?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake, then quickly squeeze it again.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up, release the front brake immediately. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: What happens to traction when you are turning?

options.text: There is less grip available for braking.
There is more grip available for braking.
Braking is the same as on a straight road.
You should never brake while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less grip available for braking.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but you must be very careful. When a motorcycle leans into a turn, some grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip for braking.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds above 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new motorcycle. Most crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when preparing to pass a vehicle on its left?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate at a higher speed. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers do not expect you there.

questions.question: What is the best thing to do if a driver is following you too closely?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only encourage them to tailgate faster.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and you operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: You should leave more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is normal. Leave more space when road conditions increase your stopping distance, such as when the road is icy or wet.

questions.question: To be more visible to other drivers, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times to be more visible. Also wear bright and reflective clothing, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and let them see you.
Be close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and let them see you.
questions.explanation: The right lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts and other drivers' blind spots. It also protects you from road hazards and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to the day, a motorcycle operator should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Leave more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgate other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance at night. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be flexible about your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more frequently than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay away from them. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If traffic is coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: To stop quickly on wet pavement, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes if you need to stop quickly on slippery surfaces. Apply the front brake gradually to avoid locking.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: The body can eliminate about one drink per hour. The time needed to lower blood alcohol content varies, so never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated by the rider's left foot.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time to stop quickly. Press them firmly and do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. Follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can make things more dangerous because they may follow you at a faster speed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A proper lane position helps you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position is important for safety. It helps you see and be seen, avoid other drivers' blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: Wearing which of the following helps protect you from serious injury, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high and sturdy boots or shoes to cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.
